newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, brief rebound expected.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, brief rebound expected.

text.p: Polish shares fell for the fourth consecutive session on Thursday but analysts said a brief rebound was possible, spurred by expectations of companies' good October earnings, most of them due on Monday.

"We will have a brief rebound - one or two sessions as some short-term investors have already started speculating before the release of the earnings reports," said Pawel Tarnowski, an analyst at Raiffeisen Capital and Investment.
The main market's WIG index fell 1.1 percent to 13,392.1, and turnover rose 16.9 percent to 84.2 million zlotys ($30.1 million) on both markets as 50 issues fell, 14 rose and 16 were flat.
Some analysts said Thursday's vote in the Senate on 1997 taxes, amending the lower house's bill seen as inflationary, could also bring some optimism to the market.
But they said the moderately lower income taxes for everyone instead of a deep cut just for the most needy could be spoiled if rejected by the lower house.
Some analysts expected the market to fall to support at 11,500 points by the end of the year.
Others said the bourse might return to its October 9 high of over 15,000 points.
Continuous trade turnover was at 0.9 million zlotys ($0.3 million) with six stocks rising, one falling and three remaining stable. Five stocks in the live trade system did not trade on Thursday.
Mass privatisation NFI units rose 4.6 percent in 16.1-million-zloty ($5.8 million) continuous trade but fell 2.6 percent in a regular session 30.9-million-zloty ($11 million) turnover.
